questions.prompt: Why is `a && b || c` NOT the same as if a; then b; else c; fi?

options.b: c also runs when a succeeded but b FAILED — || reacts to the most recent verdict

questions.prompt: A cleanup script runs `cd staging && rm -f *.tmp` (discussed, not run). What is the && buying?

options.b: if cd fails, rm never runs — without &&, rm would happily delete *.tmp in whatever directory you were actually in

questions.prompt: Under set -e (L2.2), what does `grep -q ERROR log || true` say?

options.b: 'a no-match here is fine, don't die': the || makes the failure handled, so -e lets the script continue
